sentence: This project studies how exposures within the home, such as microbial products and air pollutants, influence peanut allergy development in children.
This project tries to capture the past history of a cell by leaving a permanent genetic mark on actively transcribed genes.
This project tests whether ultrasound can switch on engineered channels in retina cells to restore vision in retinitis pigmentosa.
This project builds a microscope that shows the chemical makeup of living tissues in real time without using dyes.
This project tests whether a drug called entolimod can improve liver-directed radiotherapy and immune checkpoint blockade against liver metastasis.
This project studies how neurons in the anterior cingulate cortex and a molecule called enkephalin take part in placebo analgesia.
This project tries to find out how estrogen receptor signaling affects acute and chronic gammaherpesvirus infection, autoimmune disease and cancer.
This project uses mice to study how an adhesion class member helps synapses assemble into neural circuits in the hippocampus.
This project studies how the bacterial pathogen Legionella pneumophila exploits the ubiquitin system of its host cells.
This project studies a molecule that may control immune cell activity in hepatocellular carcinoma, a type of liver cancer.
This project provides core services and seminars to support research on intellectual and developmental disabilities.
This project designs implementation strategies and an informatics tool to handle secondary findings from whole genome sequencing, based on families' lived experiences.
This project studies how the skin microbiome and lipid metabolism work with the immune response to contribute to acne.
This project builds a shared analytical platform that measures molecules in brain tumor samples to study how tumor cells interact with the tumor microenvironment.
This project studies how biomechanical stimuli control smooth muscle cell dedifferentiation in peripheral artery disease.
This project provides brain tumor biospecimens and tests on them, such as immunohistochemistry and genomic analysis, to support brain cancer research.
This project develops computational methods that find genetic variants influencing complex disease risk and measure protein expression in specific cell types.
This project studies how protease inhibitors in mammals block viral proteases, using evolutionary biology, biochemistry and virology.
This project studies how a bone forming molecule is controlled in immune cells called macrophages in periodontal disease.
This project builds a diagnostic tool that detects glioblastoma from a blood molecular signature using globin reduction and transcriptomic profiling.
